title: Quantized model fallback canary strategy and rapid mitigation playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: After a capacity spike on 2026-02-25 we observed a regression cluster impacting quantized model variants: increased token-level accuracy drift for a subset of open-source LLaMA-derived models, and a correlated rise in unsupported-op fallbacks that caused repeated kernel fallback churn and crash loops on a small percentage of nodes. This ticket captures containment steps taken during the incident, a proposed canary + rapid mitigation playbook for future regressions, and prioritized action items to reduce blast radius and time-to-recovery.

Incident highlights:
- Window: 2026-02-25 02:10–04:05 UTC.
- Symptom A: Token-level BLEU-style accuracy regressions on quantized variants vs float baseline (median top-1 token disagreement increased from 0.42% to 1.9% on cert-prompt-set).
- Symptom B: Unsupported-op fallback spikes (op_fallback_count per-minute increased 12x) triggering repeated kernel selection churn and eventual OOM/crashloop on 4/256 GPU pods.
- Root cause hypothesis: a new fused attention kernel rolled out in runtime-2.3.0 interacted poorly with aggressive int4 packing heuristics under high-concurrency prefix workloads. The fused kernel produced subtle ordering differences that amplified on quantized scales and also uncovered an edge-case in operator fingerprinting that misclassified a subset of custom fused ops as unsupported, triggering fallbacks.

Goals of this playbook:
1) Detect regressions earlier with cross-signal alerts; correlate accuracy drift with fallback telemetry.
2) Contain blast radius by quarantining affected quantized variants and failing open to compatible float variants or older quant profiles.
3) Provide an automated, low-latency canary rollback path with safety checks and human-in-the-loop gating for high-impact customers.
4) Short-term mitigations to keep production healthy while long-term fixes (kernel revert/patch) are developed.

Files & artifacts:
- Incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-02-25+Quant+Regressions
- Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quant-ops-regressions
- PRs: runtime patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123; telemetry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/219
- Post-incident evals: gdrive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/quant-evals-2026-02
comments: 2026-02-25 03:00 UTC — Asha Patel: Initial alert from SRE: quantized serving error-rate up; some pods in crashloop. Investigated logs; saw repeated 'op unsupported' warnings followed by kernel fallback. Escalated to runtime on-call.

2026-02-25 03:25 UTC — Luca Moretti: Disabled new fused-attention kernel on the 4 affected pools (hotfix: runtime-2.3.0 -> 2.2.9) which stabilized crashloops. Live canary showed reduced fallback churn within 12 minutes. Noted that accuracy drift persisted on some variants even after kernel revert.

2026-02-25 04:10 UTC — Priya Rao (SRE): Applied temporary routing policy: route traffic for quant-int4 variants to their float equivalents for customers with SLA tier >= enterprise until canary coverage completed. This reduced customer-facing anomalies. Logged routing change: SR/2341.

2026-02-27 10:40 UTC — Merged telemetry improvements (PR #219) to include a combined signal 'quant_deviation_score' that weights token disagreement, unsupported-op_rate, and fallback_count. This signal is now available in nightly aggregates for canary alerts.
2026-03-05 16:00 UTC — Design review (Sergio Alvarez): UX needs a 'quarantine reason' field in the console when hiding variants from catalog — created follow-up DES-348 for console change.
2026-03-10 11:15 UTC — Security review: no customer data exfiltration observed; keys unchanged. Recorded as not security-impacting.

2026-03-12 09:30 UTC — Luca Moretti: Drafted automated rollback job that will: (a) detect quant_deviation_score > 0.8 for 30m, (b) mark variant Quarantined, (c) route traffic to fallback model variant, and (d) open a ticket to runtime team. PR: runtime/pull/4150. Seeking SME review from quant team.
signals: quant_deviation_score (new): weighted composite of token_disagreement_pct, unsupported_op_rate, fallback_count_per_min
action_items: Short-term (P0): automated canary rollback job (runtime/pull/4150) — implement and schedule daily dry-run; owner: Luca; ETA: 2026-03-18.
Short-term (P0): quarantine-only flag in catalog + routing rule to fail open to float variant for affected customers; owner: Priya; ETA: 2026-03-12 (completed for enterprise tier).
Medium (P1): add behavioral unit tests for fused-attention packing order on quantized models and add them to nightly canaries; owner: Jinwoo Park; ETA: 2026-03-26.
Medium (P1): improve operator fingerprinting to avoid false-positives for custom fused ops; propose safe-defer list for op types until verified; owner: Sasha Ivanov; ETA: 2026-04-08.
Medium (P2): expand telemetry retention for quant_deviation_score to 90 days to help regression hunting; owner: telemetry eng; ETA: 2026-04-01.

Long-term (P2): holistic evaluation harness that runs quantized vs float per-commit smoke tests with a subset of production prompts (~10k) and flags memory/accuracy divergence; owner: Research; ETA: 2026-Q2.
Customer communication: prepare status template and notify >affected customers with remediation plan; owner: Customer Success; ETA: 2026-03-14.
rollback_plan: If quant_deviation_score > 0.8 for 30m on canary cluster: automatically set variant state=Quarantined (console flag) and re-route traffic to configured fallback variant.
For customer-tiered protection: allow customers to opt-out of auto-fallback (enterprise may require manual approval).
If rollback job fails to complete (e.g., routing API 5xx): alert SRE with page and pause further automated actions until human triage.
Post-rollback verification: run a 15-minute smoke test against canary prompts and confirm quant_deviation_score < 0.25 before clearing quarantine.
tradeoffs_and_notes: Aggressiveness vs false positives: lower thresholds reduce blast radius but increase churning quarantines and customer-visible fallbacks. We chose a conservative composite threshold for automated action, with manual review enabled for non-critical customers.
Latency vs safety: routing to float variants increases cost and latency for some requests but preserves correctness; flagged as acceptable for short quarantine windows for safety-first customers.
Operational complexity: adding quarantine lifecycle increases state surface area (console/catalog + routing). DES-348 created to coordinate UI changes.
